Hi Andre / Maria —

Thanks again for agreeing to be a customer reference. We prepared a short case study draft (attached) and a set of localized drafts: French and Italian for the EU markets, and a Japanese version for APAC (we've attached the current machine-assisted drafts for quick review).

High level asks:
- Can you confirm the <company> branding / logo usage is OK?
- Please review the French/Italian wording and highlight any customer-sensitive language we should avoid (pricing figures, sensitive project names).
- For APAC: we'd like to check if the Japanese wording requires any regulatory qualifiers when referencing data residency / PII handling.

Timeline: we hoped to finalize by end of next week (Mar 19) so we can publish in early April. If you need more time for legal translation review, let us know expected turnaround.

Attachments: redwood_case_study_draft_en.docx, case_study_fr.docx, case_study_it.docx, case_study_ja.docx

Thanks —

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the drafts. Quick initial read: the English draft looks fine from a product perspective. A few notes from EuroTech legal/marketing:
- Please replace the specific throughput number in the third paragraph with the percent reduction we saw (we prefer relative metrics).
- In the French version there are a couple of idiomatic phrases that read oddly; I've highlighted in the attached FR file.
- For Italy: Maria will review the Italian draft for any market-specific phrasing.

One important compliance item: our legal team requires a short clause confirming that any customer logos will be used only in marketing collateral and that no internal project code names are published. If you can add that as a one-line approval checkbox in the sign-off, that should speed legal.

I'll coordinate with our translation vendor for a certified FR/IT review if needed, but we can probably do lightweight edits first.

Best,

We can do staged publishing. Our preferred path:
1) Publish the English case study on the Redwood site and a shared EU landing page (marketing-approved).
2) Lock the French/Italian localized pages behind the EU landing page and publish them once customer legal signs off (target within 2 weeks of English publish).
3) For APAC: hold the Japanese page until Kaiyo confirms regulatory phrasing — we won't publicize any claims about data residency that the customer can't confirm.

Hello Marissa / Neha —

Thank you for the draft and for checking about regulatory phrasing. A few APAC-specific notes from our legal/comms team:
- In Japan we avoid absolute statements about data location unless we can reference a specific contractual clause. Suggest: change "data stored in-region" to "configured to use customer-specified region where contractually applicable."
- Please avoid using the word "guarantee" in relation to data residency or encryption; "configured to" or "designed to" is safer.
- For customer testimonials we prefer a dual-language block (Japanese + English) when publishing on JP-facing pages.

We can approve the Japanese draft once those wording updates are made and our legal sees the sign-off clause Andre mentioned. We aim to return a formal approval by next Wednesday (Mar 18).

Regards,
Yoko Suzuki
Head of Corporate Communications
Kaiyo Inc.
